description: Principles and order of operations for sound post on a narrated documentary, radio documentary, podcast feature or archival film: audio-first ("radio cut") editing, the four-stem model (dialogue / live / music / ambience), the density ceiling, when to use silence, and which OpenDubStage skill and tool to open next. Use this whenever someone starts planning or auditing the sound of a documentary, a narrated stills film, an oral-history piece or a long-form podcast, asks "how should the sound of this be built", "what order do I do the mix in", "what are the rules for music / ambience / narration in a documentary", or wants an overview before the specific skills (dialogue-editing-and-restoration, voice-matching, music-under-narration, ambience-and-sound-for-stills, scene-transitions, mix-qc-and-delivery, ai-review-of-audio). Do NOT use for music production, game audio or live sound reinforcement.
